result.summary: Proclus summarizes the lost epic Telegony, which follows Odysseus after the Odyssey: his travels, his second marriage, and his death at the hands of his son Telegonus. A second fragment gives a different account of his children.

scenes.title: Sacrifices and Journey to Elis
scenes.summary: After the suitors are buried, Odysseus sacrifices to the Nymphs, visits Elis and Polyxenus, returns to Ithaca for Teiresias's sacrifices.

scenes.title: Thesprotian Marriage and War
scenes.summary: Odysseus goes to Thesprotis, marries Callidice and leads a war against the Brygi, where the gods clash. Polypoetes inherits the kingdom.
scenes.stakes: Odysseus's army is routed by Ares in the war.

scenes.title: Death of Odysseus
scenes.summary: Telegonus lands on Ithaca, unwittingly kills Odysseus, then takes the body, Penelope and Telemachus to Circe, who makes them immortal; the pairs marry.
scenes.stakes: Odysseus's life, defending Ithaca against an unknown attacker who is his son.

scenes.title: Alternate Genealogy
scenes.summary: Eustathius reports Odysseus's sons by Calypso and Penelope.

alias_notes.explanation: Alternative name for Odysseus's son by Calypso in fragment 2.

analysis.text: The epic extends Odysseus's story beyond the Odyssey, with a tragic irony: the wanderer is killed by his own unrecognized son.
The Telegony belonged to the Epic Cycle, and survives only in this summary by Proclus and scattered fragments.

legacy.text: The tale of Telegonus killing Odysseus with a spear tipped with a stingray spine was retold by later writers and inspired Sophocles's lost play Odysseus Acanthoplex.

fun_facts.text: Eugammon of Cyrene is dated to about 568 BC, making the Telegony one of the latest poems in the Epic Cycle.

language_notes.text: Chrestomathia means a collection of useful passages; Proclus' summary of the Epic Cycle is the main source for this lost poem.
A mixing bowl (krater) was a large vessel in which wine was blended with water, a typical guest-gift.
Trophonius and Agamedes were legendary builders, and Augeas the king of Elis with the filthy stables; the poem digresses to their stories.
The sacrifices ordered by Teiresias refer to the prophecy the seer gave Odysseus in the underworld in the Odyssey.
The Brygi are a people of the northern Greek region; here they are enemies of the Thesprotians.
Unwittingly means without knowing; Telegonus does not recognize his father.

context_notes.text: Eugammon of Cyrene composed the Telegony, the last poem of the Epic Cycle, probably in the sixth century BC.
The Nymphs were female nature spirits of springs and caves; Odysseus honored them in Ithaca.
Ares is the god of war, Athena a war goddess of strategy, and Apollo the god who here ends their fight.
Circe is the sorceress of the Odyssey who detained Odysseus and is Telegonus' mother.

literary_notes.text: Gods fighting among mortals echoes the divine conflicts of the Iliad.
The audience knows the stranger is Odysseus' son, while father and son do not, making the killing tragic.
Death is followed by immortality and unexpected marriages, resolving the tragedy with a surprising, almost fairy-tale reversal.
